title: Admissibility of the identity point morphism
statement: Fix the global finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\Qlb$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and an integer $n\geq1$; put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $a_s=\operatorname{id}_s$. Use the small pro-etale coefficient categories and the identity compactification $s\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}}s\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}}s$. Then $a_s$ is exceptional-adjoint admissible at every finite coefficient stage in the sense of [def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility], with $c_{\mathrm{cd}}=0$ in [def-weil-full-cohomological-dimension] and $c_f^-=c_f^+=0$. The ambient compact-support functor and its right adjoint are naturally identified with the identity functor, with identity unit and counit. Under these identifications, the adjunction data agree under all compactification refinement comparisons. The finite-reduction and scalar-extension comparisons for these right adjoints are the identity transformations of the corresponding coefficient-change functors. The bounds are uniform in the coefficient stage, so the same morphism is admissible at $\mathcal O_E$, $E$, and $\Qlb$.

source.place: paragraph, sentence 5 counting the semicolon clauses as the item's steps do: 'The identification of $R\mathcal H om_s$ with $R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda$ is [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point].' The node makes precise the hypothesis needed to obtain this identification from [lem-pod-point-dualizing-complex] in the conventions [def-pod-conventions] at the auxiliary point $X_0=\operatorname{Spec}k_0$; the blueprint sentence itself does not mention admissibility

proof.text: Take the scheme base $S=s$; the identity is separated, finite type, proper and an open immersion directly from these definitions, and $\ell$ is invertible since $\ell\ne p$. Put $A=A_{E,n}$ and $D_T=D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$. For any scheme $T$, the formula $(f_*M)(V)=M(V\times_YX)$ of [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image], with $f=\operatorname{id}_T$, identifies $f_*$ naturally with the identity: $V\times_TT\cong V$, compatibly with restrictions and the constant-ring action. It is exact. In the construction [def-weil-derived-direct-image], a quasi-isomorphism $K\to I$ to a K-injective complex then gives $R(\operatorname{id}_T)_*K=I\cong K$; this is the natural identity identification of [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition]. Also extension by zero for $\operatorname{id}_T$ in [def-weil-extension-by-zero] is the identity, since every test object factors through $T$ and the presheaf being sheafified is already $M$. Thus the chosen identity compactification has compact-support candidate $F_0=R(\operatorname{id}_s)_*\operatorname{id}_!\cong\operatorname{id}_{D_s}$ by [def-weil-compact-support-candidate].

source.place: identity compactification; explicit identity direct-image and extension-by-zero computations

proof.text: Check both clauses of [def-weil-full-cohomological-dimension] for its chosen proper part $p=\operatorname{id}_s$. For any module sheaf $M$, step 1 gives $Rp_*(\iota_sM)\cong\iota_sM$. Its cohomology in degree $r>0$ is zero, since the complex has only its degree-zero term; use the kernel/image description in [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. For every object $v:V\to s$ of the pro-etale site, $s\times_sV\cong V$ and $p_V$ is the identity under this canonical identification. Apply the very same calculation on $V$ to the pulled-back sheaf $g_V^*M$: $\mathcal H^r(R(p_V)_*(\iota_Vg_V^*M))=0$ for $r>0$. This does not require $V$ to be finite type or the sheaf to be constructible. Hence $\operatorname{FullCD}(\operatorname{id}_s,A;0)$.

source.place: full cohomological dimension at the identity and all pro-etale base changes

proof.text: Let $d=(s\xrightarrow{j_d}Z_d\xrightarrow{p_d}s)$ be any compactification in [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. The relation $p_dj_d=\operatorname{id}_s$ makes $j_d$ a section of $p_d$. Properness includes separatedness by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-section-separated-closed-immersion] applies and makes $j_d$ a closed immersion. It is already an open immersion, so its image and its complement are disjoint open subschemes covering $Z_d$. The section identifies its image with $s$, with inverse the restriction of $p_d$.

source.place: Tag 01KT (schemes-lemma-section-immersion): closed-immersion assertion for a section of a separated morphism

proof.text: For the open-and-closed $j_d$ of step 3, the definitions [def-weil-extension-by-zero, def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image] identify $j_{d!}M$ with $j_{d*}M$. Indeed each test scheme $W\to Z_d$ is covered by the two disjoint opens $W_s=W\times_{Z_d}s$ and $W_C$ over the complement. The sheafification defining $j_{d!}M$ has restrictions $M$ and zero on these two pieces, and gluing gives $M(W_s)\times0=M(W_s)=(j_{d*}M)(W)$. This is natural in both $W$ and $M$. The same two-piece gluing identifies module sheaves on $Z_d$ with pairs of module sheaves on its two open pieces; morphisms and their kernels and cokernels are computed in the two components. Hence the inclusion $M\mapsto(M,0)$, namely $j_{d*}$, is exact. Applying it to a quasi-isomorphism $K\to I$ preserves that quasi-isomorphism, so the K-injective formula [def-weil-derived-direct-image] gives the canonical identification $j_{d!}=j_{d*}\cong Rj_{d*}$ on all of $D_s$.

source.place: elementary sheaf gluing on the two clopen pieces; all ambient complexes

proof.text:
For every $d$, combine step 4 with the finite-level composition isomorphism of [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition] to obtain a natural isomorphism
$$\beta_d:F_d=Rp_{d*}j_{d!}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_{d*}Rj_{d*}\xrightarrow{\sim}R(p_dj_d)_*\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{id}_{D_s}.$$
Here $F_d$ is exactly the ambient candidate of [def-weil-compact-support-candidate]. For a refinement $u:d\to e$, $uj_d=j_e$ and $p_eu=p_d$. Steps 3–4 and the same composition theorem identify $Ru_*j_{d!}\cong Ru_*Rj_{d*}\cong Rj_{e*}\cong j_{e!}$ on the whole ambient category. Use this isomorphism and proper composition to define $\theta_u:F_d\xrightarrow{\sim}F_e$. Associativity and the identity laws in the cited theorem give $\beta_e\theta_u=\beta_d$, since both paths are the inverse composition comparison for $p_euj_d=\operatorname{id}_s$. Thus $\theta_u=\beta_e^{-1}\beta_d$, $\theta_{\operatorname{id}}=\operatorname{id}$ and $\theta_{vu}=\theta_v\theta_u$. This establishes the needed ambient comparisons directly for this morphism.

source.place: identity adjoint assertion: compactification comparisons via the clopen section

proof.text: For each $d$ choose $G_d=\operatorname{id}_{D_s}$. Define the adjunction $F_d\dashv G_d$ by the natural bijection $h\mapsto h\circ\beta_{d,K}^{-1}$ from $\operatorname{Hom}(F_dK,L)$ to $\operatorname{Hom}(K,L)$; its inverse is $a\mapsto a\circ\beta_{d,K}$. The unit is $\eta^d_K=\beta_{d,K}^{-1}$ and the counit is $\varepsilon^d_L=\beta_{d,L}$. In the identification $F_d\cong\operatorname{id}$ both are identities. Set $\rho_u:G_e\to G_d$ to be the identity. The refinement equations of [def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint] now read $\beta_e^{-1}=\theta_u\beta_d^{-1}$ and $\beta_d=\beta_e\theta_u$, which are step 5. The composition equations for $\theta$ were proved there and those for $\rho$ are identities. Together with step 2 this supplies the full ambient datum for the chosen compactification. If an already chosen right adjoint is used instead, [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] gives its unique counit-compatible natural isomorphism to this one; hence the assertion is about canonical adjunction identifications, not a literal equality of independently chosen models.

source.place: identity is its own right adjoint; units, counits and all refinement equations

proof.text: In the identity model $G_0L=L$, so a bounded constructible object in $D_c^{[a,b]}(s,A)$ has exactly the same cohomology and remains in that interval [def-weil-constructible-intervals]. For every sheaf $M$ in degree zero the complexes $(G_0L)\otimes_A^LM$ and $L\otimes_A^LM$ are identical; therefore every Tor-amplitude interval for $L$ is unchanged [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Both properties are invariant under the natural isomorphism of step 6. Consequently clauses (2) and (3) of [def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility] hold with $c_f^-=c_f^+=0$, while clause (1) is steps 2 and 6.

source.place: the preservation clauses with zero shifts

proof.text: Let $T$ be any of the finite-reduction or scalar-extension functors between coefficient stages. At $s$ the source and target coefficient-change functors are the same $T$. In the identity models of the preceding steps, the left-functor comparison is $T\operatorname{id}=\operatorname{id}T$, with component $1_{TL}$: on a K-flat representative $P$, the geometric coefficient comparison for the identity sends $P\otimes B$ to the same $P\otimes B$ by the identity. The right-adjoint comparison is its mate: the transpose of $T(\varepsilon_L)$ composed with the inverse left comparison. Both factors are identities, and transposition in $\operatorname{id}\dashv\operatorname{id}$ is the identity on the Hom set. Its component is therefore $1_{TL}$, also when $T$ is not exact before deriving it. Identity and successive-change diagrams commute because their arrows are identities after the specified coefficient-change identifications. The point stages in [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] are kept separate: at integral coefficients the identity preserves the derived-complete category, at $E$ it acts identically on the rationalized objects and morphisms, and at $\Qlb$ it acts identically on every common finite-stage representative. The bounds $0,0,0$ above do not depend on $E$ or $n$. The last paragraph of [def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility] therefore gives admissibility at $\mathcal O_E$, $E$ and $\Qlb$ as claimed.
